# Lesson Plan — Organic Chemistry Unit Opener: Carbon Bonding

> Class: chemie_9b_2026_27
> Date: 2026-07-09
> Duration: 45 min

## Learning goals
- Connect prior redox/electron-transfer language to electron sharing in organic chemistry.
- Explain that carbon commonly forms four bonds using simple molecule examples.
- Compare methane, ethane, ethene, and ethyne visually without overloading orbital terminology.

## Lesson flow
- **Redox bridge** (15 min): quick recap of oxidation/reduction as electron transfer.
- **Carbon bonding models** (20 min): draw methane and ethane, then use model kits.
- **Contrast examples** (7 min): show ethene and ethyne as visual double/triple-bond contrasts.
- **Exit ticket** (3 min): explain electron sharing versus electron transfer.

## Warmup
- Ask students to recall oxidation as electron loss and reduction as electron gain.

## Practice tasks
- Build methane and ethane with molecule kits.
- Sketch the same molecules from the board model.
- Compare one single-bond and one double-bond example visually.

## Homework
- No homework planned yet.

## Teacher notes
- Keep hybridization language light; use concrete molecule examples first.
- Watch for confusion between oxidation numbers and actual charges during the recap.
